headline: High: CrewAI’s broad filesystem/network/tool access can amplify shared-context marketing skills into prompt injection, leakage, and unsafe downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI reads/writes the host working directory and uses shared memory with developer-defined state, so attacker-controlled content can be fed into its agent loop. marketingskills explicitly says skills “reference each other and build on shared context,” which creates an instruction-hijack pathway if CrewAI ingests those files or outputs. No direct shared channel is documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF CrewAI loads skill files or workspace text as instructions, injected directives can steer agent behavior.
IF marketingskills content is placed into CrewAI shared context, one agent can influence the other’s tool use.
mitigations: Separate instruction files from data files in distinct directories.
Add a fixed system prompt that ignores file-embedded instructions.
Require human review before executing any tool call derived from workspace text.
Use read-only mounts for untrusted skill content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles API keys and broad network egress, while marketingskills exposes local skill files and shared context. If both run in the same workspace, CrewAI can read files and transmit their contents to model providers or configured tools, leaking marketing content or secrets. The pairwise path is plausible in default setups, but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable workspace, CrewAI can read marketingskills files from disk.
IF CrewAI forwards workspace text to model providers or tools, file contents can leave the host.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate workspace directory.
Disable network egress for runs that process sensitive files.
Store secrets outside any shared working directory.
Review outbound tool/API destinations before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and both support multiple instances. CrewAI also executes shell/subprocesses broadly, while marketingskills references shared context files. Without explicit locking or isolation, concurrent writes to the same workspace can clobber files or corrupt shared state. The overlap is real in default configurations, but not enough for high because git state and unrestricted shared-dir writes are not both documented.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF both agents run concurrently without locks, shared context files can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate output directory.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Make shared files read-only during execution.
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent runs.
requires-engineering: add transactional state management.

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is an orchestration framework that can treat tool outputs as inputs for later agents, and marketingskills explicitly builds on shared context. That makes it plausible for one agent’s generated marketing claims to be reused by the other without verification. The blast radius is multiple work products rather than direct irreversible harm, so medium is the best fit.
conditions: IF CrewAI passes generated text into marketingskills without validation, errors can propagate.
IF marketingskills reuses prior agent output as authoritative context, hallucinations can cascade.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before reuse of any generated claim.
Require source links for factual assertions.
Limit shared context to summaries, not raw outputs.
Have a human approve externally visible copy.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking against source data.

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles API keys and broad network egress, while marketingskills is a marketing-content skill set with local skill files. No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, so only a low compliance risk is supportable. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of content and outbound transmission.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into CrewAI prompts or marketingskills files, retention and residency controls may be implicated.
IF outbound model-provider calls process regulated content, policy mismatches can arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Review vendor retention settings before use.
Use redacted sample content for testing.
Document where prompts and outputs are stored.
requires-engineering: add data-class routing controls.
